BLOGS


September 30, 2026


####


Rohith Kori


SVP, Product Strategy | Agilysys


***Hospitality technology leader with 15+ years of industry experience***
Connect with Rohith in[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rohithkori/)


#### **Key Takeaways**


- Governance transforms AI from isolated success stories into repeatable business outcomes by establishing consistent standards, accountability, and oversight across the organization.


- Far from slowing innovation, governance accelerates AI adoption by providing a common framework that allows new capabilities to be deployed with confidence and consistency.


- As AI evolves into a digital workforce that can influence decisions and workflows, governance becomes essential for defining boundaries, maintaining control, and enabling AI to scale responsibly.


Every successful hospitality organization relies on foundational operating disciplines.


Financial controls ensure accountability. Service standards help deliver consistent guest experiences regardless of property, location, or employee. Revenue management practices guide pricing decisions and profitability. Brand standards ensure that every property reflects the same promise and identity.


Together, these disciplines create the structure that allows organizations to operate confidently and predictably as they grow. They establish clear expectations and provide a repeatable approach that can be applied throughout the operation.


The same principle applies to AI. Demonstrating value is only the first step. Maintaining that value as AI expands across the business requires the same level of structure and oversight that supports every other part of the operation.


Governance provides that structure.


#### **Governance is More Than Compliance**


[In our previous post](https://www.agilysys.com/en/blog/trust-the-foundation-of-ai-adoption-in-hospitality/) , we explored why trust is the foundation of AI adoption in hospitality. Trust allows organizations to begin their AI journey with confidence. But as AI becomes embedded across guest experiences, operational workflows, and business decisions, organizations need a way to ensure that the same standards can be applied as adoption expands.


Many people hear the word governance and immediately think about compliance reviews, legal approvals, or security requirements. Those things are important—and in many cases required—but governance is much broader than that.


Governance is the mechanism that enables organizations to grow with AI.


> ”
>
>
> Governance creates a repeatable operating model that spans how AI is used across the business and defines how information is accessed, how recommendations are generated, how decisions are reviewed, and how accountability is maintained without requiring every team to reinvent processes.


Governance provides the discipline that turns isolated successes into repeatable outcomes. As AI continues to grow into its role in hospitality, governance becomes a foundational requirement. It is not optional.


#### **Governance Creates Repeatability**


Most organizations do not struggle to find opportunities for AI; the opportunities are everywhere. AI can help personalize guest experiences, automate repetitive work, surface operational insights, and support better decision-making.


The challenge is turning those opportunities into repeatable outcomes. A hospitality organization may be able to manage a single AI initiative through manual oversight and informal processes. But as AI expands across departments, properties, employees, and guest interactions, that approach quickly becomes difficult to sustain.


This is where governance creates value.


Without governance, organizations often implement AI in silos. Different systems use different models. Different approaches emerge for how AI is managed and evaluated. Each solution develops its own processes and controls.


Over time, that fragmentation becomes a barrier. What works in one department may be difficult to replicate in another. Visibility becomes limited. Testing becomes inconsistent. Teams spend time focusing on foundational capabilities rather than delivering value.


Governance establishes the standards that determine how AI is used throughout an organization. It provides a common foundation that allows successful approaches to be applied consistently as adoption expands and additional AI capabilities are introduced. Successful outcomes become easier to reproduce. AI initiatives become easier to expand.


Governance also helps ensure that the value created from an organization’s information remains aligned with their goals and objectives. Hospitality operators invest heavily in understanding their guests, refining operational practices, and building institutional knowledge. Governance helps establish clear expectations around how that information is used so that it continues to create value for the business that generated it.


Governance creates repeatability. Repeatability is what makes scale possible.


#### **Why Governance Accelerates Innovation**


Repeatability delivers something equally important: confidence. When organizations know that standards are being applied consistently and that information is being handled appropriately, they become more comfortable expanding AI into new areas of the business. That confidence becomes a catalyst for innovation.


> ”
>
>
> One of the most common misconceptions about governance is that it slows innovation. In reality, the opposite is often true. Organizations scale by establishing common standards that create consistency across the business. The same principle applies as AI adoption expands.


Without governance, every AI initiative can evolve differently. Different approaches emerge for handling information, reviewing recommendations, and managing oversight. As adoption grows, that inconsistency becomes increasingly difficult to manage. By establishing common standards and shared approaches, organizations can focus less on rebuilding foundations and more on identifying new opportunities to improve guest experiences and operational outcomes.


In many ways, governance allows organizations to approach AI with greater confidence. New capabilities can be evaluated against established standards rather than starting from scratch each time. Adoption becomes easier because the organization already has a framework for how AI should operate within the business.


Effective governance provides the structure organizations need to scale innovation with confidence, without introducing unnecessary bureaucracy.


#### **Governing the Digital Workforce**


The importance of governance will only increase as AI evolves from supporting decisions to actively participating in operational workflows. As AI becomes more deeply embedded into hospitality operations, the nature of governance begins to evolve. Increasingly, AI systems are beginning to take actions, coordinate workflows, and influence decisions across the organization.


One useful way to think about this evolution is through the lens of a new employee. When a new employee joins your team, you do not immediately allow them to make million-dollar decisions. You establish processes, checks, balances, and oversight mechanisms. This allows your business to efficiently scale because common procedures create consistency, accountability, and oversight across departments.


This thinking should also apply to AI. It may be helpful to view AI-enabled systems as “digital employees” participating in the operation. Depending on the role they play, they may function much like a front desk associate, a controller, a revenue manager, or even a CFO—analyzing information, making recommendations, and increasingly acting on behalf of the organization. The same operational controls that exist for human employees must also exist for digital employees; however, a critical difference is that digital workers operate much faster than human workers. That means governance controls must evolve to match the speed at which those digital workers operate.


> ”
>
>
> As digital workers become more capable, governance must evolve as well. Organizations must understand not only what digital workers can do, but also what they should be allowed to do. This will increasingly require automated controls that can operate at the speed and scale of the systems being governed, while preserving the human judgment needed to ensure AI remains aligned with business objectives.


Much like any employee entrusted with important decisions, digital workers require clear boundaries, accountability, and oversight.


#### **Trust Enables Adoption. Governance Enables Scale.**


Trust allows organizations to begin their AI journey with confidence. Governance allows them to scale it.


AI initiatives rarely struggle because organizations lack ideas or opportunities. More often, they struggle because successful outcomes cannot be reproduced consistently across the business.


Governance creates the structure that turns isolated successes into repeatable outcomes. It provides the confidence needed to expand AI across departments, properties, workflows, and guest experiences. And it becomes most effective when the technologies supporting those experiences operate in a cohesive ecosystem with a common framework of accountability, oversight, and decision-making.


The organizations that create the greatest value from AI will not necessarily be those with access to the most advanced models. They will be the organizations that can apply AI consistently, responsibly, and at scale. Because at scale, AI success is determined less by models and more by discipline. Governed AI is the only AI that scales.


Written By


Rohith Kori


As Senior Vice President of Corporate and Product Strategy, Rohith leverages 15+ years of technology leadership to deliver innovative property management, POS, and payment solutions for global hospitality enterprises.
